items.title: Breaking: Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor reportedly arrested
items.description: Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor has been arrested on suspicion of misconduct in public office, the BBC has reported.

items.title: Visual clues show the US could be getting closer to attacking Iran
items.description: The steady flow of military assets moving towards Europe and the Middle East appears to be a warning that the US could be ready to attack Iran.

items.title: Accused High Country killer Greg Lynn applies for bail
items.description: The former Jetstar pilot awaits a retrial for the murder of Carol Clay, after his 2024 conviction was quashed in December.

items.title: Hanson plays into meme status, Taylor goes on tour
items.description: This week, the new opposition leader revealed his shadow cabinet while Pauline Hanson spun through a cycle she knows well.

items.title: Coles manager admits dog food price moves were outside 'guardrails'
items.description: A second Coles manager has been grilled in the federal court over whether rushing a product onto a "Down Down" promotion could have broken internal guidelines.

items.title: SA secures Australian MotoGP, world-first street circuit announced
items.description: The South Australian government has confirmed the Australian MotoGP will move to Adelaide from 2027, bringing with it huge economic benefits, but the opposition and Greens say the state has other priorities.

items.title: Live: Aussies among first competitors in newest Olympic sport
items.description: Skimo, the newest sport at the Winter Olympics, makes its grand arrival in Milan Cortina, while Australia's teenage sensation Indra Brown hits the half-pipe. Follow live.

items.title: In her memoir, Gisèle Pelicot reveals the man she kept hidden
items.description: The world knows Gisèle Pelicot as the woman who waived anonymity during France's most infamous rape trial. But in her new memoir she reveals an unexpected story — the boyfriend she kept hidden and the love that helped her face an open courtroom.

items.title: How Australia has the power to ban 'ISIS brides' from returning
items.description: One of the Australian women being held in a Syrian refugee camp has been barred from returning home after being given a temporary exclusion order — but the ban may not be as temporary as the name implies.

items.title: How the deadliest US avalanche in 40 years unfolded
items.description: Eight back-country skiers have been found dead and one is missing after an avalanche near Lake Tahoe in California, officials say.

items.title: South Korea's ex-president Yoon Suk Yeol sentenced to life over insurrection
items.description: Former South Korean President Yoon Suk Yeol is sentenced to life in prison on charges of rebellion for his attempt to put the country under military rule.

items.title: Childcare provider fined $35k after neurodivergent boy wanders off
items.description: One of Australia's biggest providers of before-and-after-school care penalised after a five-year-old neurodivergent child escapes supervision unnoticed.

items.title: Charlie Pickering on his ADHD, satire and the 'ludicrous' Trump era
items.description: Political satire occasionally comes at a price, but Charlie Pickering still believes the right joke at the right time can have a huge impact.

items.title: Gas explosion kills 16 as apartment building collapses in Pakistan
items.description: Women and children are among 16 people killed after a gas explosion ripped through an apartment building in Pakistan on Thursday.

items.title: Extremist material allegedly found on man's phone after vehicle stop
items.description: A 31-year-old has been arrested a second time after police stopped and searched a vehicle in Yagoona and seized three mobile phones allegedly storing violent extremist material.

items.title: Best International Film Oscar-hopefuls finally hit Australian cinemas
items.description: Australians will also finally be able to catch Sirât and The Voice of Hind Rajab, two movies that will be vying for Best International Film at the Academy Awards next month.

items.title: A heartwarming tribute for 'a great human'
items.description: This Winter Olympics aerials competition saw plenty of Aussies achieve lifetime goals, but they never forgot the one person who was missing.

items.title: 'Religious leader' allegedly controlled lives of youth group, court told
items.description: An alleged religious leader accused of "controlling every aspect" of the lives of a Venezuelan youth group has been granted release on strict home detention conditions by a South Australian court.

items.title: Collingwood apologises after asking elderly members to donate via their wills
items.description: The Magpies have come under fire after a letter campaign asking elderly members to amend their wills to donate to the AFL club.

items.title: Senate committee features climate disinformation and Dr Karl's clash with One Nation
items.description: The scourge of AI-slopaganda, viral disinformation campaigns and online attacks against individuals and institutions is going to get far worse before it gets better, if the latest public hearings on the topic are any indication.

items.title: Malinauskas criticised over aged care workforce comments
items.description: South Australia's Premier Peter Malinauskas has been criticised across the political divide for comments he made asking One Nation voters "who's going to feed you and bathe you and wipe your bum when you're 90", but a government spokesperson says the comments have been mischaracterised.

items.title: 'There were no cowards': Bombing of Darwin commemorated 84 years on
items.description: Eighty-four years after Darwin was bombed in the single largest foreign attack ever mounted on Australian soil, hundreds of people have gathered to remember.

items.title: Salmon farm antibiotics found in native species
items.description: An antibiotic used by the Tasmanian salmon farming industry is detected in native species more than 10km away from the closest fish operation using it.

items.title: Australian-first remotely piloted police drone trial raises surveillance questions
items.description: Police will control drones from more than 600 kilometres away from a rural town battling high crime rates.

items.title: Australian couple trapped in Argentina with no legal rights to biological child
items.description: Jonathan and Amy had a child via surrogacy in Argentina. They have been stuck there for 12 months, unable to bring their daughter home.
